text:
Score: 5/10.

I would not approve this as-is. The code is generally readable and the small pure unit tests pass, but the advertised tiny end-to-end path fails because the source story dataset is missing. The HuggingFace path also has weak guardrails and the preference workflow does not really implement pairwise preference scoring as documented.

Verification run:
`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider` -> 6 passed, 1 failed at tiny extraction due missing `data/stories/manifest.json`.
Precomputed-vector validation and steering commands against `outputs/tiny_demo/vectors` both ran successfully.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: about 175 lines, excluding adding the missing story data itself.

issues.description: Default story path points to data/stories, but the repo contains no manifest or story files, so extraction and demo runs fail.
Story loading hard-requires manifest.json and every story file with no generation or fallback despite the documented runnable tiny demo.
The end-to-end tiny test currently fails with FileNotFoundError for data/stories/manifest.json.
Documentation says the system can load or generate stories and scores pairwise preference logits, but neither behavior is implemented.
The documented tiny CPU demo is not reproducible from the checked-in repo because required source data is absent.
pca_components_for_variance(threshold=0) still returns one component instead of zero components.
project_out_components treats all-zero or rank-deficient component rows as real axes and can remove arbitrary signal.
Validation trusts vector artifacts but constructs the backend from CLI config, with no backend, layer, or dimension compatibility checks.
Preference steering also lacks artifact/backend compatibility checks before comparing loaded vectors to live backend activations.
HF preference_logit scores one activity via a good-minus-bad continuation logit, not a pairwise preference between activities.
Elo ratings are derived by pairwise-comparing scalar activity scores rather than actual pairwise model preference logits.
HF scoring assumes ' good' and ' bad' encode to usable first tokens and never validates tokenizer output.
Context validation can crash or emit NaN metrics when manifest emotions have no or insufficient matching built-in scenarios.
Extraction assumes every configured emotion has loaded stories and will fail later with KeyError or stack errors instead of validating inputs up front.
Config values are parsed lazily without validating nonempty emotions, positive scale counts, or valid workflow combinations.
Test instructions omit installing the test extra, so a fresh environment may not have pytest even after the documented base install.
